expansion:
Corneal topography is the keyed answer because the lecture names it directly as the tool for mapping corneal shape and curvature: screening for corneal ectasia (a disease of abnormal curvature) is described as "MANDATORY before refractive surgery (corneal topography)" (L15,16, page 22), and the keratoconus diagnosis section states its topographic sign explicitly — "Topography: inferior steepening, asymmetric bowtie pattern" (L15,16, page 24). Topography works by mapping the anterior corneal surface point by point and displaying the resulting curvature as a colour-coded map, which is exactly what is needed to detect the irregular, steepened curvature of a diseased or ectatic cornea.

Pachymetry, option A, measures corneal thickness, not curvature; it is used alongside topography in refractive-surgery and ectasia screening (for example to confirm an adequate residual stromal bed), but it reports a single thickness value rather than a shape or curvature map, so it cannot substitute for topography when curvature specifically is the question (not taken from the course material for pachymetry's definition, though the lecture uses it as a companion screening test).

Gonioscopy, option C, examines the anterior chamber angle using a mirrored contact lens to assess structures such as the trabecular meshwork; it does not image or measure the anterior corneal curvature at all, and is used for angle and glaucoma assessment rather than for corneal shape (not taken from the course material).

Biometry, option D, measures ocular dimensions — principally axial length and (via keratometry, a related but distinct measurement) average corneal power — mainly to calculate intraocular lens power before cataract surgery; it yields a single average curvature/power value rather than the detailed point-by-point curvature map that topography provides, so it is not the tool used to characterise corneal curvature in detail (not taken from the course material).
objective: Identify corneal topography as the investigation that maps corneal curvature, as used in keratoconus diagnosis and pre-refractive-surgery screening
